title: Democrats Outline Affordability and Anti-Corruption Agenda for New Congress
dek: After winning control of Congress in the midterms, Democratic leaders say they will focus on costs and oversight, while the Iran war and a divided government shape what can pass.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The west front of the United States Capitol building in Washington, D.C.

keyPoints: Democrats ran on lowering costs and stamping out corruption, and now hold the majority, according to NPR.
CNBC reported that party leaders plan legislation on affordability while seeking to rein in President Donald Trump through oversight.
ABC News and Politico reported that Democrats plan both a legislative agenda and an investigative track.
NPR reported the party must unite a sometimes fractious caucus to deliver on its pledges, with Trump still in the White House for two more years.
body:
Democrats who won control of Congress in the midterm elections are laying out an agenda built on lowering costs and increasing oversight of the executive branch, party leaders and reporting from several outlets said.

## Affordability first

NPR reported that Democrats campaigned on lowering costs and stamping out corruption. CNBC reported that congressional Democrats are preparing legislation on affordability.

## Oversight track

ABC News reported that Democrats have signaled they will pursue an investigative track alongside legislation, which they say is meant to restore a congressional check on the executive branch. Politico reported that the party must also confront how to legislate with President Donald Trump still in office for the next two years.

## Obstacles

NPR reported that the party's leaders will have to unite a caucus that it described as sometimes fractious. Scripps News reported that Democrats also vowed to address the ongoing war in Iran alongside their anti-corruption push.

## What we do not know

The reports do not give a timetable for specific bills, and the outcome of votes in the new Congress is not yet known.

## Divided government ahead

Reporting from several outlets frames the next two years as a period of divided government. Democrats will hold the House and, according to NPR, control of Congress overall, while Trump remains in the White House with the veto power that comes with it. Any bill that reaches his desk will need either his signature or a veto-proof margin that the reports do not describe as available.

## Process questions

Politico reported that the party's next challenge is turning campaign promises into legislation under those conditions. The reports reviewed do not describe which committees will move first, or whether leadership plans to prioritize oversight hearings before major bills. That sequencing is one of the open questions for the coming months.

## Background for readers

The affordability message was central to the campaign, and the anti-corruption message was tied to the Iran war and to scrutiny of the executive branch. Both themes appear in the agendas outlined by CNBC, ABC News and NPR. Meridian will track formal legislative schedules and committee assignments as they are announced.
